items.title: The huge Elegoo Black Friday sale includes $80 off the 3D printer we most recommend for beginners
paragraphs: If you've been waiting for the right 3D printer deal to start exploring this exciting craft, Black Friday is your moment. The Elegoo Black Friday sale is in full swing, and the Centauri Carbon 2 Combo, a machine we highly recommend for beginners, is reduced by $80 to $369 at Amazon.

We think this is an ideal choice for beginners since it's easy to set up and run, offers good value and provides plenty of flexibility to grow as a creator since it can handle a range of materials and multi-colour printing (see our guide to the best 3D printers to see how it compares to other options we've tested). There are also a couple of great deals running on Elegoo resin printers if you want to make more detailed objects, and the brand's running discounts on resins and filaments.

For most beginners, an FDM (fused deposition modeling) 3D printer is the way to go. They're safer, cleaner, cheaper to run, and easier to post-process than resin printers. We recommend the Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo because as well as making things as easy as possible, it provides plenty of versatility to dive deep once you're ready to start getting more hands on and to develop in 3D printing, without having to go out an buy another machine that allows more flexibility.

It leaves very little work to do in assembly, with no gantries to bolt together. You just remove the accessories and shipping foam, plug in the screen, and you can be up and running in a few minutes. It offers a practical mid-size build volume of 256 × 256 × 256mm (10.1 × 10.1 × 10.1 inches), the closed frame means you can work with a wide range of materials and there's the option of multi-colour printing.
There's also a built-in camera, so you can film timelapses of your print jobs and monitor in real time, and it has a self-clean function.

My exception to this recommendation would be if you specifically want to create detailed miniatures or character models, which require ultra-fine precision and a higher surface quality. For that, the best-value introduction is the Mars 5 Ultra.

Joe is a regular freelance journalist and editor at Creative Bloq. He writes news, features and buying guides and keeps track of the best equipment and software for creatives, from video editing programs to monitors and accessories. A veteran news writer and photographer, he now works as a project manager at the London and Buenos Aires-based design, production and branding agency Hermana Creatives. There he manages a team of designers, photographers and video editors who specialise in producing visual content and design assets for the hospitality sector. He also dances Argentine tango.

items.title: Which gaming headsets are worth the cost? I put 20 to the test – here are the best for 2026
paragraphs: We talk a lot about graphics in video games; we know how important it is to play on a decent screen so we can see what we’re shooting at … or running away from. But what about sound? Explosions, dialogue, the wheezy breathing of a nearby monster – arguably, audio quality is just as important.

Many modern games now support 3D or spatial audio, which lets you detect exactly where a sound is coming from in the game world. In survival horror adventures, you can hear the zombie lurking in the next room, and in popular shooters such as Fortnite and Apex Legends, you can pinpoint the footsteps of approaching enemies.

Sadly, most of us can’t afford elaborate surround sound speaker systems for our living rooms, but that’s where gaming headsets come in. They not only let you play without disturbing anyone else in the house (or office), but are also brilliant for spatial audio. I’ve tested an array of models to suit most budgets and needs, and, hopefully, with my help, you’ll never be surprised by a zombie again.
Best gaming headset overallSteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni
Best budget gaming headsetTurtle Beach Atlas 200
Best for multiplayer gamesRazer BlackShark V3 Pro
Best for comfortCorsair Void V2 Max Wireless
Best gaming headset for audiophilesAudeze Maxwell 2 ANC

I have been playing video games for 45 years and writing about them for my entire career as a journalist, so I really understand what makes a good piece of gaming hardware. During that time, I have reviewed hundreds of joypads, monitors, keyboards and, yes, headsets, developing a range of tests to sort the quality gear from the overpriced gimmicks.

I tested 20 headsets, paying close attention to comfort, which is vital for long gaming sessions, as well as sound quality, noise-cancelling capabilities and any other special features. As someone who plays video games every day for a living (it’s a tough job, etc), I was able to put every headset through hours of testing with a variety of games. I wore them while blasting strangers in Call of Duty, scoring volleys in EA Sports FC and building scale reproductions of Norman castles in Minecraft.

I also made sure I was getting good spatial information to detect exactly where my next opponent/victim was coming from. And naturally, the microphone has to make your voice crystal clear when talking to (or yelling at) teammates in the heat of battle.

To gauge the overall build quality, I put them through the ultimate trial: lending them to my teenage sons. If anything came back in one piece, I knew it was well constructed. My aim was to find headsets that felt light yet sturdy, sounded good, and aided – maybe even improved (if that’s possible) – my gaming performance.
Once tested, the headsets were donated to SpecialEffect, a charity that makes video games accessible to people with disabilities.
What we loveImmersive sound; excellent compatibility and comfort
What we don’t loveExpensive and can get sweaty

Danish manufacturer SteelSeries makes a range of highly acclaimed headsets, and this is the centrepiece of its collection, featuring 40mm drivers, active noise cancellation (ANC) and a high-bandwidth omnidirectional microphone for clear, natural speech. Instead of a basic USB dongle for connecting to a PC or console, it comes with a base station that plugs into your games machine and lets you tweak your sound settings via a monochrome screen.

Why we love it As soon as you load up a game, you know what you’re paying for. The Nova Pro Omni produces a lovely wide soundstage, making you feel immersed in the environment. While playing Elden Ring, I really felt the rumble of dragons flying overhead and the whoosh of arrows whizzing past my ears. The ANC is effective, easily filtering out the electric fan in my games room. The mic made my shouts of “There’s a sniper on that rooftop!” easily discernible to my Call of Duty teammates, but also picked up regular chatter with decent clarity. It’s comfortable, too, with plump earcups finished in a soft vegan leather, and the adjustable suspension band nicely cushions your head. It also uses neodymium, a compact, lightweight and highly magnetic material, in its drivers, reducing the headset weight while also producing precise, detailed sound.

It’s the base station that sets the SteelSeries apart. There are three USB ports at the back, so you can plug in a PC, PlayStation and Xbox simultaneously and easily switch between them (you can also connect your phone via Bluetooth if you want to watch TikTok videos while you’re waiting for a game to load). There’s even a charging port in the side for the removable battery that powers the headset. Better still, two rechargeable batteries are included in the box, so you’ll never run out of juice in the middle of an all-day Minecraft session.
For tinkerers, free smartphone and PC apps let you intricately modify the sound settings or choose from hundreds of preset options designed for specific games.

It’s a shame that … the earcups did get sweaty after several hours of Warzone, and it’s expensive. But if you have a PC and/or multiple consoles and want decent movie and music performance all from one headset, it’s definitely worth it.

Compatibility: PC, Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, mobile Weight: 339g (with mic arm attached Battery life: up to 30 hours per battery Drivers: custom 40 mm neodymium magnetic ANC: yes Sustainability: SteelSeries says all its products have parts that can be recycled and repurposed, and it sells replacement parts such as new earcups and headbands
What we loveImmersive sound; excellent compatibility and comfort
What we don’t loveExpensive and can get sweaty
What we loveCovers all the basics at an affordable price
What we don’t loveMaterials feel cheaper and more brittle than competitors

Turtle Beach is among the best-known brands in the gaming headset world, and it’s a master of affordable-yet-hardy models. The Atlas 200 comes in three variations: multiplatform (PC, mobile and Xbox), PlayStation and a dedicated PC version that comes with a USB adaptor providing 24-bit resolution high-fidelity sound and support for the Waves 3D audio processing technology. It’s a no-nonsense wired headset with bass-loving 50mm drivers and a flip-to-mute mic, which means you just lift it up into its upright position to turn it off.

Why we love it At 280g, this is a light headset and comfortable to wear. The headband puts barely any pressure on your skull, and the earcups have good cushioning, yet dissipate heat well. I wore it for hours without it feeling sweaty or heavy. The sound is a little crunchy and unrefined, but it does the job, and it handles spatial audio reasonably well, although I found it difficult to tell if ambient sounds were above, below or on the same level as me. The mic is clear. While the Atlas 200 can’t compete with top-end models, it’s incredible value, outperforming other budget models. And it lasts surprisingly well: my sons have owned Atlas headsets for years, and somehow they’re still functioning. It’s a great option for casual gamers who just want a reliable headset they can throw on and forget about.
It’s a shame that … the mesh fabric that covers the headband feels fragile, but for the price, we’re not complaining.

Compatibility: PC, PlayStation, Xbox and mobile Weight: 280g Drivers: 50mm Nanoclear ANC: no Sustainability: Turtle Beach has reduced plastics in its packaging and claims on its website to be using post-consumer recycled plastic in some of its products. It sells spare parts for its current headsets
What we loveCovers all the basics at an affordable price
What we don’t loveMaterials feel cheaper and more brittle than competitors
What we loveExcellent performance for competitive online games
What we don’t loveQuite expensive and EQ presets are limited

I’m a big fan of Razer, and my trusted neon green Kraken headset is still going after five years of heavy use. The BlackShark V3 Pro is the company’s high-end model, aimed at esports athletes (and wannabes), featuring ANC, a large detachable boom mic and 50mm drivers. It’s built for long sessions – lightweight but very comfortable with soft, breathable fabric covering the cups. If you are getting continually blasted by 12-year-olds in Fortnite, it’s not because your ears are too sweaty.

Why we love it The sound is punchy and precise, allowing you to catch every distinct rumble, roar or intriguing snippet of dialogue, no matter where it’s happening. Want to hear a pin drop in your game world? You’ve come to the right place. The default setting is tuned toward higher frequencies (perfect for footsteps), but a button lets you select from a range of pre-set EQ (equalisation) levels designed for specific games or for movie watching.

If you pair the headset with Razer’s apps (Razer Audio and Razer Synapse), you can customise all the EQ settings yourself. The mic is crisp, reliable and actively suppresses background noise, and there’s a handy scroll wheel to fine tune the mix of game sound and chat volume. The buttons are tactile and easy to use while playing. You can also connect to your phone via Bluetooth to take calls and view social media. The BlackShark V3 Pro feels like a high-end piece of sports equipment – like an expensive tennis racket or a pair of fancy football boots – in the same way, they will make you aspire to be a better player.
It’s a shame that … I could never get the sound just right for listening to music, but that’s a small issue. The dongle is on a weirdly long lead, too.
Compatibility: separate models for PC, PS5 and Xbox Weight: 367g Battery life: up to 70 hours Drivers: 50mm ANC: yes Sustainability: headset contains 24.67% post-consumer recycled (PCR) plastic
What we loveExcellent performance for competitive online games
What we don’t loveQuite expensive and EQ presets are limited
What we loveComfy to wear for long periods; great sound
What we don’t loveAll-plastic build; fixed boom mic; teen-focused design

Sitting comfortably in the mid-range of prices, Corsair’s Void V2 Max Wireless is a lightweight model styled with teen gamers in mind. It features 50mm drivers and support for Dolby Atmos spatial audio, and the boom mic can be flipped up or down to switch it on and off. There are four ready-made EQ settings such as Bass Boost and FPS (first-person shooter) Competition, which accentuates the sound of footsteps and gunfire, accessible by pressing down on the volume button. You can also use Corsair’s iCue app to customise the EQ and mic settings, as well as tweak the colour patterns of the snazzy RGB lighting on the earcups.

Why we love it For a start, it’s comfortable. The earcups are made of a particularly soft, squidgy memory foam, and they’re roomy, which helps to keep you cool through long periods of play. On top of this, the Void Max produces a surprisingly complex, textured audio experience with hefty bass that doesn’t impede higher-frequency sound effects.

The boom mic is nice and clear, too, although it’s a shame you can’t remove it. Plus, there’s Bluetooth support so you can connect to your phone and listen to Spotify – or take calls – while piloting a F-15 Strike Eagle in Ace Combat 8. My 18-year-old son grabbed this headset as soon as it arrived and absconded with it, so he’s definitely a fan.
It’s a shame that … it’s plasticky, so don’t sit on it. Also, the flashing RGB strips are not for everyone.

Compatibility: PC, PS5, Nintendo Switch, mobile. Separate model for Xbox Weight: 303g Battery life: up to 70 hours Drivers: 50mm ANC: no Sustainability: a Corsair spokesperson said: “Corsair does not take products back for recycling. Corsair offers a two-year warranty for all our gaming peripherals. If the headset is not operating in accordance with its published technical specifications, it will be replaced at Corsair’s expense. We offer replacement parts such as earpads, USB dongles and charging cables; these are complimentary, and you just need to pay for shipping unless it is under warranty.”
What we loveComfy to wear for long periods; great sound
What we don’t loveAll-plastic build; fixed boom mic; teen-focused design
What we loveSuperb sound and noise cancellation
What we don’t loveHeavy; clunky styling; expensive

Designed for gaming audiophiles, the Maxwell 2 uses 90mm planar drivers rather than the more common dynamic drivers. While the latter use a vibrating cone to produce sound, planar drivers use a thin diaphragm, which produces a more precise, authentic sound with less possibility of distortion. To accommodate them, the earcups are rather large – my son said they look like dumbbells, but thankfully they’re not quite as heavy. It comes with an app if you want to tinker with the sound levels, and you can connect to your phone via Bluetooth to listen to music.

Why we love it If you take pride in your high-end PC and widescreen 4k monitor, you want a headset to match – and this is it. The Maxwell 2 has absolutely gorgeous sound, achieving eardrum-bludgeoning bass, but also lots of mid- to high-frequency detail and a wide acoustic space for a truly cinematic feel.

Playing sci-fi shooter ARC Raiders, I could hear the wind whistling above me, the thudding footsteps of giant killer robots and the distant pings of far-off gun fights – all with impressive spatial precision. It also supports head tracking (with the relevant software and compatible games), for even more accuracy. The noise cancellation is very good, easily blocking out my noisy PC and the TV blaring in the next room, and the mic is so clear, I sounded like I was recording a podcast. A serious and sublime headset.

It’s a shame that … it is heavy, although the wide suspension band helps take the pressure off. When connected to a gaming device via the wireless dongle and a mobile phone via Bluetooth, the headset automatically prioritises audio sources. Users can’t manually switch between the two wireless audio sources or listen to both simultaneously.

Compatibility: available in separate Xbox/PC and PlayStation/PC versions. Both versions also support Mac, Nintendo Switch, Switch 2 and mobile devices. Weight: 560g Battery life: up to 40hrs Drivers : 90mm planar magnetic ANC: yes Sustainability: Regarding repairs, a spokesperson said that if it’s an easily replaceable part, Audeze will provide it to customers. If not, it will ask the customer to send in the headphones to be repaired. Repairs are free under warranty, but customers may need to cover postage costs for any needed beyond 30 days of purchase
What we loveSuperb sound and noise cancellation
What we don’t loveHeavy; clunky styling; expensive
What we loveExcellent audio, and comfortable
What we don’t lovePricey for a wired headset

For those who just want a straightforward headset that gets the important stuff right, the MMX 300 Pro is the perfect option. It’s a wired model with impressive sound, deep bass and accurate spatial detail, and the mic is crystal clear. As you’d expect from a company specialising in studio headphones, it’s wonderful for music too.

The soft, velvety earcups are comfortable, so you can wear the headset for hours, and I like the accessible in-line controls for the mic and volume, so you don’t have to fiddle with the headset mid-game. I tested the closed-back MMX 300 Pro, but if you’d prefer an open back, consider the MMX 330 Pro. Beyerdynamic also has cheaper models – including the wireless MMX 130 and MMX 230 – that are extremely good too.
It didn’t make the final cut because … there are slightly more feature-rich options at the price.

Compatibility: PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch and smartphone; Weight: 314g; Battery life: not applicable, wired only; Drivers: 45mm Stellar 45 dynamic; ANC: no; sustainability: the earpads, headband and cable can all be easily replaced, but the company provides no specific recycling guidance
What we loveExcellent audio, and comfortable
What we don’t lovePricey for a wired headset
What we loveA light, bright and well-priced wireless headset
What we don’t loveMic lacks fidelity; there’s better audio quality elsewhere

At 212g, this is one of the lightest headsets I tested, but it’s resilient and comfortable thanks to the flexible plastic frame and soft memory-foam earcups. It offers both 2.4 GHz wireless connectivity and Bluetooth, so you can use it with your PC, any console and a smartphone, and the sound quality is decent with strong detail and an acceptable oomph to the bass. The volume controls are on switches rather than a dial, which isn’t ideal, but I found the buttons big and tactile, so they’re easy to find by touch. All in all, a great-value wireless headset.
It didn’t make the final cut because … the mic is embedded in the ear cup, so it’s not quite as clear as headsets with a boom mic attached.

Compatibility: PC, PS5, Nintendo Switch and mobile; Weight: 212g; Battery life: more than 24 hours; Drivers: 32mm dynamic; ANC: no; Sustainability: no specific information on this headset, but Logitech claims to be implementing sustainability initiatives, including using recycled plastics and ensuring products can be easily disassembled and recycled by the consumer. Spare parts and guides are available via the Logitech Repair Hub
What we loveA light, bright and well-priced wireless headset
What we don’t loveMic lacks fidelity; there’s better audio quality elsewhere
What we loveStrong audio performance and supreme comfort
What we don’t loveSimilar to Nova Pro Omni, but I prefer that model’s warmth

The flagship model in the Turtle Beach range has rich cinematic sound (certified Hi-Res by the Japan Audio Society), while picking out those all-important footsteps and other environmental signals via excellent implementation of Dolby Atmos spatial audio. I tested with the epic adventure Ghost of Yōtei and loved how it captured the swirling winds, crackling fires and clashing blades – it was like being inside a Kurosawa movie.

Owners of multiple gaming systems can easily switch between four devices, including PC, PS5, Xbox and smartphone, and the supplied base station charges one of the two supplied batteries so you never run out of power. Add in the powerful ANC, extremely good detachable mic and comfortable, sturdy build, and you have a truly top-end headset.
It didn’t make the final cut because … the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni is marginally better, but it’s close.

Compatibility: PC, PlayStation, Xbox (Xbox-specific model) and smartphones via Bluetooth; separate models for Xbox and PS5/PC; Weight: 393g; Battery life: up to 40 hours per battery; Drivers: 60mm Eclipse Dual; ANC: yes; Sustainability: see Turtle Beach Atlas 200
What we loveStrong audio performance and supreme comfort
What we don’t loveSimilar to Nova Pro Omni, but I prefer that model’s warmth
What we loveRefreshingly soft styling with decent sound
What we don’t loveFlimsy compared with similarly priced rivals

In a market filled with identical black headsets, the Nova 3 offers a selection of lovely soft colours such as lavender and aqua. It’s a comfortable option too, with an adjustable suspension strip beneath the headband and gentle fabric earcups.

Even the audio is mellow, providing a nicely balanced sound stage that allows you to pick out important noises without being blasted by a wall of bass. As well as the usual 2.4GHz low-latency wireless connectivity via an included USB-C dongle, it also offers Bluetooth connectivity for your smartphone, and you can easily switch between them, just in case you fancy some TikTok action between Fortnite scuffles. There’s also an app to access custom EQ settings for different games.
It didn’t make the final cut because … there’s strong competition in this price range, and it’s so delicate my sons were worried they’d break it.

Compatibility: PS5, PC, Nintendo Switch, Xbox and mobile devices; Weight: 253g; Battery life: up to 30 hours; Drivers: 40mm neodymium magnetic; ANC: no; Sustainability: see info on Arctis Nova Pro Omni
What we loveRefreshingly soft styling with decent sound
What we don’t loveFlimsy compared with similarly priced rivals

The first decision you’re likely to make is between a wired and a wireless headset. The former tends to be a little cheaper; they’re also convenient and don’t require batteries. Wireless headsets free you from the tyranny of cables and often offer a range of connectivity options, including the standard 2.4GHz radio frequency, which will require a dongle receiver to be plugged into your PC or console, and Bluetooth for your smartphone. They do introduce a tiny amount of latency (the delay between your game generating a sound and you hearing it), but it is extremely low (about 10 milliseconds) in modern headsets.

Another key decision is whether to buy open-back or closed-back headphones. The former have grills or holes in the back of the ear cups to allow sound to move through and create a more natural audio experience. Closed-back headphones tend to create a seal around your ears so sound can’t escape: they’re better for booming bass and privacy, but can create distorted extraneous sounds – and make your ears hot. Most gaming headsets are closed-back, and this would be my recommendation for most gamers, as they put you right inside the virtual environment with no distractions. Many also offer active noise cancellation (ANC), a technology that emits sound waves to counteract and reduce incoming noise – great if you’re playing in a loud environment.

Audio quality is dictated by the drivers, which sit in each earcup, turning electric signals into sound waves. They come in different sizes, ranging from 40mm to 90mm, with the latter being the loudest, but not necessarily the best. Smaller drivers cope better with high frequencies, so they’re good for hearing footsteps; larger drivers provide heavier bass, so they’re great for games with pounding soundtracks or lots of cool explosions. Another important specification is frequency response, which is the range of audio frequencies a headset can reproduce: gaming headsets are usually in the 20–20,000 Hz range.

Spatial sound is important because it immerses you in the game world and helps you locate nearby enemies or loot chests – the good news is that many headsets support it, because the processing is done by the PC or console via software such as Dolby Atmos or Windows Sonic. However, accuracy is affected by the driver quality and the acoustic tuning in the headset. Some headsets come with apps that let you fine tune the range of the frequencies within the audio signal – ie the EQ (equalisation) settings – so that you can boost the bass, mid-range or treble.

Decent headsets that offer acceptable comfort, build quality and audio start at about £40 for a wired model and £60 for wireless. At about £100-£150, you’re getting a headset made with better materials and higher-quality drivers, as well as other features such as Bluetooth connectivity for your phone. At the top end, £250 upwards, you can expect highly configurable, studio-quality audio, supreme comfort and often the ability to connect to multiple consoles, switching seamlessly between them.

The problem with headsets is that they have a lot of delicate parts. They’re quite an intimate piece of equipment. Earcups will trap grease, sweat and skin particles from previous users, so unless these can be replaced, it’s unhygienic, to say the least. Also, you won’t know whether they’ve been looked after well simply from looking at a photo online. If you’re determined to buy secondhand on a site such as eBay, make sure the seller has excellent feedback and offers returns so you can inspect the headset when it arrives. Otherwise, look at stores and marketplaces such as Back Market or CEX that offer warranties on used goods.

Alternatively, Corsair sells refurbished headsets on its website. Honestly though, if money is an issue, I’d rather buy the best new budget or mid-range headset I can afford rather than a secondhand model with no warranty and an unknown hygiene history.
For more, read the best TVs for every home and the best gaming chairs for comfort and support

Keith Stuart is a veteran video game journalist with 30 years’ experience of testing, rating and breaking hi-tech gadgets. He has been wearing gaming headsets almost every day throughout his career, much to the frustration of anyone else in the house who needs to speak to him

items.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
paragraphs: The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

Wilson’s talk on 23 November, titled “Little Black Stretchy Pants” after his memoir, was billed as an “intimate, fireside chat” offering insight into the “mind and instincts of the man himself”. It was moderated by Nuvyn Peters, CEO of Axis Connects.

There is no publicly available video of the event, but the Guardian spoke with people who attended it and reviewed social media posts from those present. Outrage over the event was first reported by the Globe and Mail.

According to people who were there, Wilson told the audience that companies would be reluctant to hire a 22-year-old woman because she might become pregnant at 23 and take maternity leave. He went on to suggest that women were waiting too long to have children, prompting men to import brides from Thailand.
“There were audible gasps in the room and everyone was clearly uncomfortable. It was a mix of disengaging, walking out and also just complete shock of what was being said on stage,” one person said.

“I am floored that Axis gave this man a platform. We all were saying before the event it was surprising he was there – and it’s clear that [Wilson] runs in the organizer’s circles after she opened with the fact that they go on walks [at a Vancouver mountain] together.”
The event, which was supposed to run for an hour, was cut short at 45 minutes.

The remarks are not the first time Wilson has attracted criticism for his comments about women and their bodies. He stepped down as chair of Lululemon’s board in 2013 after the company’s signature black yoga pants were criticized for being see-through and Wilson blamed the problem on the body types of some customers.
On Monday, he reportedly told the group that those prior comments about body types had been “misconstrued” and said he was referring to women who wear sizes that are too small.
Wilson, who is believed to be worth more than C$6bn, has not had a leadership role at Lululemon for several years but remains a major shareholder.
He also reportedly told the audience that poverty had largely been eradicated, and that he was looking forward to going to space with Elon Musk.

Audience members also said Wilson suggested that men were better suited to helm clothing companies that catered to women, because they knew what looked good on women’s bodies. He said the same was true of women who lead companies focused on men’s fashion.

“We recognize that several comments made by Chip Wilson at the Leadership Forum were offensive and inconsistent with the values and mission of Axis Connects,” Peters said in a statement. “We understand why those remarks caused concern and disappointment among members of our community. His comments also underscore an uncomfortable reality: attitudes and assumptions that hold women back in the workplace and in leadership have not disappeared. Challenging those attitudes is central to the work and ethos of Axis Connects.”

Wilson’s spokesperson pointed to the work the Lululemon founder has done to mentor and “empower” women in leadership roles over the years and said his efforts “speak for themselves”. A number of women who were early employees of the company and worked closely with Wilson became millionaires when the company went public, he has previously noted in his memoir, and have gone on to found their own businesses.

More than 700 women attended the conference, many representing organizations they worked for. One person said the experience left her “irate”, adding that it was also indicative of what women continued to tolerate.
“It’s just sad that this is what women still have to deal with, in a forum literally for women.”

items.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
paragraphs: Smoke appears after explosion heard in Iowa near Army detonation site

The US military has hailed as a "huge success" the detonation of nearly five tonnes of toxic explosives in Iowa, an operation that sparked widespread fears of health and environmental problems across the region.
Smoke was seen rising into the sky shortly after 09:00 local time (14:00 GMT) following the explosion, as the Army declared the risk "as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible".
President Donald Trump said reports showed mitigation efforts "far exceeded expectations".

Plans to detonate the lead azide, a highly volatile compound reportedly at risk of exploding on its own, were paused multiple times before Wednesday's detonation following public outcry and legal challenges.
Despite widespread concern from residents of Middletown, Iowa, ahead of the blast, officials have said that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.
"The Army's controlled, mitigated detonation exceeded all expectations and was a HUGE success," Adam Telle, acting secretary of the US Army, wrote on social media.
"We are watching EPA's [Environmental Protection Agency] MASSIVE sensor array throughout the area closely, and there are no readings so far above 0.0," he added.

The explosives had been in storage for around 20 years, and degraded as part of a process known as recrystallisation - this made them more responsive to accidental detonation from friction or other movement.
No level of lead exposure is considered safe, with children and pregnant women particularly vulnerable to harmful effects.
Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson told the BBC he felt "relieved" and "vindicated" after the detonation.
He watched the blast from his job at a manufacturing plant eight miles (12km) away from the blast - and monitored a camera at his two-bedroom home just one mile from the detonation site.
"We did not feel anything. We did not see anything," Johnson said.
Also eight miles away from Middletown, Sandy Mabeus closed the windows and the garage at her home, brought their outdoor cat inside and hunkered down.
The family watched three separate live streams on iPads and televisions of the explosion as it happened.
"We did not feel or hear a thing here," she told the BBC, adding that she checked the videos to confirm it had actually happened.
"The waiting and wondering has not been a good thing for anybody in the area," she said. "Hopefully they had a very good result and we can just get on with things."

Iowa farmer David Vandenberg lives about 20 miles from the blast site and said he first learned of the detonation around two weeks ago. The Army Corps of Engineers took samples from his yard and pond on Tuesday.
"I was listening this morning, and I did hear a rumble about nine o'clock," he told the BBC on Wednesday, but didn't see or smell anything.
Vandenberg expects officials to return to take more samples but "was happy to see that the blast was relatively contained. "I think the effects will be minimal"
Iowa's incoming Governor-elect Rob Sand said there was "more testing to do" and called for "immediate transparency" to explain why the lead-up was "so chaotic and unclear".
Sand said that any Iowans who have been impacted in any way "must be taken care of fully, right away".
Cameron Hamilton, administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), said there would be additional resources and testing in the coming days and weeks.
In recent weeks, the US Army scheduled and rescheduled their detonation ahead of colder winter temperatures.

It also warned locals of "potential exposure to toxic lead dust", which led to some panic. It instituted measures including an optional evacuation zone and a shelter-in-place advisory ahead of the detonation.
The Army faced pushback from residents and politicians alike and there were legal challenges to prevent the detonation from going ahead on environmental and health grounds.
But on Monday, the appeals court overturned a decision to halt the blast. It said that - while these concerns were valid - the risk from an unplanned explosion was greater.
Sheila Flynn and Kwasi Gyamfi Asiedu contributed to this report

items.title: UN warns Afghan women face deepening risks on the international day for the elimination of violence against women
paragraphs: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Dari article.

The United Nations on Wednesday issued a renewed warning that Afghan women and girls are facing growing risks of violence while essential services meant to support them are shrinking because of funding cuts.

The statement was released by U.N. Women Afghanistan to mark the start of the global 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence and the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women

It urged governments and donors to increase support for Afghan women's organizations, describing them as an essential lifeline for women and girls living under mounting social, economic and humanitarian pressures.

“Just as the risks of violence against women and girls are growing, the services they depend on are disappearing because of aid cuts,” said Susan Ferguson, U.N. Women’s Special Representative in Afghanistan.

The annual campaign, observed worldwide from November 25 to December 10, comes as Afghanistan remains at the center of international concern over women's rights. U.N. Women says restrictions imposed on women and girls, combined with poverty,
displacement and shrinking humanitarian funding, are leaving many increasingly vulnerable to violence and abuse.
This year's campaign is being held under the message “Still together. Stand with Afghan women and girls.”
According to U.N. Women, the funding crisis is forcing organizations that provide support to women and survivors of gender-based violence to scale back or cease operations altogether.

The agency says more than 193 service points for survivors of violence have closed across Afghanistan this year because of aid cuts, affecting more than one million women and girls. Nearly 300 humanitarian health facilities have also been suspended or shut down, reducing access to healthcare for women in many parts of the country.
U.N. Women estimates that up to 427,000 women could soon lose access to services ranging from counseling and legal support to vocational training and safe spaces.
Since returning to power in August 2021, the Taliban have imposed a series of measures limiting women's access to education, employment, public spaces and other aspects of public life.
U.N. agencies report that more than 100 decrees and directives affecting women and girls have been issued over the past five years.
Taliban officials have consistently said women's rights in Afghanistan are protected in accordance with Islamic law and Afghan cultural values.

A U.N. assessment released earlier this year found that women in Afghanistan are nearly four times less likely than men to access formal justice mechanisms, leaving many without effective avenues to seek protection or report abuse.

Addressing a U.N. event marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, U.N. Women Executive Director Sima Bahous said weak justice systems and shrinking support services continue to leave survivors vulnerable worldwide.
“Justice means a survivor safely seeking help, and our institutions protecting her, ensuring her access to justice, and holding perpetrators to account,” Bahous said.
The start of the campaign also comes amid growing international efforts to recognize the treatment of Afghan women and girls as “gender apartheid.”
Human rights advocates argue that the systematic exclusion of women from education, employment and public life amounts to institutionalized gender-based segregation.

Earlier this month, Amnesty International Australia called on Canberra to support international recognition of gender apartheid as a crime under international law and to support accountability efforts related to Afghanistan.

Most recently, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot announced that France would support efforts to define and punish gender apartheid as an international crime, specifically citing the segregation of women and girls in Afghanistan.

items.title: Iraqi Kurdistan faces renewed pressure on its autonomy from Baghdad and Tehran
paragraphs: Washington, Sulaimaniyah, Iraqi Kurdistan —
Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Kurdish article.

Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered federal authorities to take control over all border crossings in the semi-autonomous Kurdistan Region and to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control in four provinces, a move Kurdish leaders rejected as unconstitutional.

However, Iraq’s Federal Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that Baghdad has the constitutional authority to deploy federal forces along all international borders, including those in the Kurdistan Region, lending judicial backing to al-Zaidi’s efforts to expand federal authority.

The orders, issued Tuesday, follow an investigation into oil smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company. Baghdad says the measures are aimed at combatting smuggling and protecting national resources, but Kurdish officials say they threaten the region’s constitutionally recognized autonomy.
The measures announced by Al-Zaidi include deploying federal security personnel, closing unofficial crossings, and expanding surveillance of oil production and transportation.
Sabah al-Numan, spokesperson for the commander-in-chief of Iraq’s armed forces, told VOA that the decisions were part of an ongoing investigation into oil smuggling.
Combatting oil smuggling is certainly among the government’s priorities,” al-Numan said.
Abdul Amir Taiban, an adviser to the Iraqi prime minister, told VOA that investigations had uncovered smuggling operations involving national resources, prompting the federal government to intervene.

Taiban defended Baghdad’s actions, citing Articles 110 and 112 of Iraq’s constitution, which define the federal government’s exclusive powers and its role in managing oil and gas. “The federal government is continuing to complete its measures to put an end to theft, violations and encroachments on national wealth,” he said, calling on the regional government to comply with the constitution.

The Kurdistan Regional Government’s Council of Ministers on Wednesday rejected Baghdad’s measures, saying the constitution requires joint management of oil resources and protects the region’s authority.

Iraqi constitutional expert Maytham Handhal told VOA that ambiguities in the constitution itself have contributed to recurring disputes between Baghdad and Erbil, the capital of Iraq’s semi-autonomous Kurdistan Region.
He told VOA that adopting a federal oil and gas law could provide a framework for resolving disagreements over production, management and revenue distribution.

Iraqi political analyst Ihsan al-Shammari warned that the deployment of federal forces in Kurdish-controlled areas, alongside unresolved disputes over salaries, budgets and oil revenues, could trigger another crisis between Baghdad and Erbil.
Mahmoud Khoshnaw, a member of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan, told VOA that Baghdad’s decisions would create new tensions but also could provide an opportunity to address outstanding disagreements.
He described the absence of a federal oil and gas law as the “missing link” in resolving the dispute and stressed the importance of continued dialogue with Baghdad.

The dispute with Baghdad comes as the Kurdistan Region faces renewed military pressure from neighboring Iran, which has justified operations against Iranian Kurdish opposition groups on security grounds.
Officials from the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan told VOA that eight separate drone attacks targeted camps and facilities in Erbil and Sulaymaniyah provinces Tuesday night.
The officials said they suspect Iran was responsible. VOA could not independently establish who carried out the attacks.
Amanj Zibayi, a senior Democratic Party official, said the strikes were intended to intimidate residents and prevent them from returning to the camps.

items.title: US UN ambassador calls flogging of singer Parastoo Ahmadi: 'pure medieval barbarism'
paragraphs: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Persian article.
U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz condemned the flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi for performing music without the mandatory hijab.
Writing on the social media platform X, Waltz stated: "Punishing singer Parastoo Ahmadi and her crew with 74 lashings for a YouTube performance without a hijab is pure medieval barbarism."

Commenting on the Islamic Republic, Waltz added: "While the regime in Tehran tries to deflect, its brutality leaves it completely isolated. The United States stands with the Iranian people against this tyranny."

The condemnation followed an announcement on Monday by defense attorney Mostafa Nili, who reported that the flogging sentences against Parastoo Ahmadi and four crew members of the "Caravanserai Concert" had been carried out at the Qom Prosecutor's Office.
According to Nili, Parastoo Ahmadi, Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amirali Pirnia, and Mohsen Lashgari each received 74 lashes after their convictions were upheld.

The case stems from a musical performance at the historic Deir-e Gachin Caravanserai in Qom province, a video of which was published on YouTube on December 11, 2024, under the title "Caravanserai Concert."
In addition to the flogging, the five artists were sentenced to a two-year ban on artistic and musical activities and a two-year travel ban.

Amnesty International had previously called for a halt to the floggings, stating that the punishment constitutes torture, but Islamic Republic authorities carried out the sentences despite international outcry.

items.title: BBC appeals against decision to allow Trump's $10bn lawsuit to go ahead
paragraphs: The BBC has lodged an "urgent" appeal against a US judge's decision to allow Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.6bn) lawsuit against the corporation to go ahead.
The US president is suing the BBC for defamation over the way an episode of Panorama edited a speech he gave in January 2021, shortly before the riot at the US Capitol.
Earlier this month, a federal judge in Florida ruled that the defamation case could proceed after the BBC sought to dismiss it.

The BBC has now filed an appeal with a higher court, saying there is a "complete lack of evidence" that anyone in Florida accessed the programme, and that the broadcaster made "rigorous and systematic efforts to prevent access to the documentary" in the US.
A BBC spokesman said: "We are surprised and disappointed by the court's decision that this case should be heard in Florida.
"As we have made clear from the start, the BBC broadcast this documentary in the UK - and UK only. We did not show it in Florida, nor did any other broadcaster.
"Given the urgency of this issue, we are now requesting a higher court review the ruling."
President Trump's lawsuit accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave on 6 January 2021.
The BBC has apologised for the edit in Trump: A Second Chance, which it said had given "the mistaken impression that President Trump made a direct call for violent action".
But the corporation argued that the Panorama episode, which was broadcast in 2024, did not meet the legal criteria for defamation.
Earlier this month, federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz found Trump's defamation allegations against the BBC sufficient for the case to continue, although he did not rule on the merits of the case.
President Trump called the judge's ruling a "huge victory" in a post on Truth Social at the time.
The BBC has now lodged an appeal with the US Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, arguing that the Florida court has no jurisdiction to hear the case.
Trump has been ordered to answer questions under oath as part of the lawsuit by 22 January.
Judge Kuntz has scheduled a trial date for the case for 3 May 2027 in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

items.title: China investigates Shanghai Party chief in latest blow to political elite
paragraphs: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Mandarin article.
In an unexpected move, China has placed Shanghai Communist Party chief Chen Jining — a member of the ruling party’s Politburo — under investigation, ahead of a major leadership reshuffle in 2027.

The official Xinhua News Agency reported Tuesday that Chen, 62, is under investigation for “suspected severe violations of discipline and laws" but gave no further details. He is being investigated by the Communist Party's top anti-corruption watchdog.

Chen is the fourth member of the 24-member Politburo chosen in 2022 to be investigated, after Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui and two top military officials, Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, all seen as close to Xi.

The investigation is notable because of the post that Chen holds. Shanghai’s party secretary is one of China’s most powerful regional posts and has traditionally served as a steppingstone to the highest levels of the Communist Party. The last time a Shanghai Party Chief was investigated was Chen Liangyu in 2006.
President Xi Jinping, Premier Li Qiang and former leader Jiang Zemin all held the position before rising to national leadership.

Chen entered the Politburo in 2022 and was appointed as Shanghai party secretary shortly afterward, replacing Li Qiang, who had been promoted to the Politburo Standing Committee, the party's most powerful decision-making body.
A trained environmental scientist, Chen earned a doctorate from Imperial College London in 1992 and later served as president of Beijing's prestigious Tsinghua University from 2012 to 2015.
He entered government in 2015, serving as China's environmental protection minister before becoming mayor of Beijing in 2017. He oversaw preparations for the 2022 Winter Olympics.

Unlike many senior Communist Party officials whose careers have been built primarily through political and administrative networks, Chen was widely regarded as a technocrat with strong academic credentials and expertise in science and technology.

The announcement caught many China watchers by surprise. Chinese authorities have not disclosed specific allegations or evidence against Chen. The wording, “suspected severe violations of discipline and laws,” is commonly used in corruption investigations.
Yang Jianli, founder of the U.S.-based human rights organization Citizen Power Initiatives for China, told VOA that anyone perceived as a potential successor to Xi could become a political target.
"Xi Jinping cannot allow another center of power to emerge while he is trying to extend his rule and accomplish his political ambitions," Yang said.
Chen's case comes amid an intensifying campaign against senior officials across China's civilian and military leadership.

Neil Thomas, an honorary senior fellow on Chinese politics at the Asia Society Policy Institute, described the investigation into Chen Jining as the latest step in Xi’s campaign of “self-revolution,” the party’s term for strict internal discipline.

“Xi believes strict internal discipline is essential to transform the CCP [Chinese Communist Party] into an effective self-regulating institution that avoids the fate of the Soviet Union and escapes China's historical cycle of rising and falling dynasties,” he wrote on X.

At the Chinese Communist Party's Fifth Plenum in October, the party announced the expulsion of 33 Central Committee members, the largest such purge at a single plenum since China's reform and opening-up period began in 1978.

The 21st Communist Party Congress is expected to convene in Beijing in the second half of 2027. Xi already has broken with the party's previous practice of limiting leaders to two five-year terms, and he is widely expected to seek an unprecedented fourth term as party chief.
Thomas said further purges are likely before the congress, as Xi seeks to promote a new generation of officials whose loyalty to him is beyond question.

items.title: Desai Chia designs Bethesda Residence to balance "openness and discretion"
paragraphs: A large light well brings daylight deep into this private home that was designed by Desai Chia Architecture for a tight site in a dense Maryland neighbourhood.
The project takes its name from its location in Bethesda, a city located northwest of Washington DC.

The house is set within a suburban neighbourhood near the downtown district, where residential lots are about one-fifth of an acre (647 square metres). Because the houses here are close together, the architects needed to be very mindful of privacy concerns.
“The clients sought a house that would feel open and light-filled without sacrificing privacy,” said New York-based Desai Chia Architecture.
“Its compact lot and the close proximity of neighbouring houses required a careful response balancing both openness and discretion.”
The architects intended the house to “rethink suburban-urban hybrid living through a modern lens”.
Roughly rectangular in plan, it has three levels and a basement. Setbacks help break up the mass, particularly on the street-facing elevation.
The building appears “as a two-storey building from several vantage points,” the team said.
“The home is carefully scaled to blend with neighbouring houses, balancing a strong architectural identity with sensitivity to its suburban context,” the team said.
Facades are clad in grey fibre-cement panels made to last for a century. The material is known for protecting against fire, pests and extreme weather, according to the team.
“A durable, low-maintenance exterior with a strong architectural presence was a key client priority from the outset,” the architects said.
“Glass-fibre-reinforced concrete (GRFC) panels were selected to create a crisp, sculptural facade that captures texture and shifting light throughout the day.”
A modern-style bay window adds dimension and visual interest to the front and back facades.
Within the home, public spaces are located on the ground level. The rear portion opens into a yard with a lap pool.
The upper levels contain bedrooms and two offices, and the top floor has a rooftop terrace. The basement holds a gym, ping-pong area and media room.

A limited number of windows helps ensure privacy. To provide natural illumination, the team created a three-storey light well, which is positioned along a central staircase and brings daylight deep into the dwelling.

“This vertical, faceted volume allows sunlight to cascade downward, distributing diffuse light from a small skylight across circulation spaces on multiple levels while minimising solar heat gain,” Desai Chia Architecture said.
The all-electric house has a geothermal heating and cooling system. To enable the homeowners to age in place, the house has a shaft where an ADA-compliant elevator could be added in the future.
The homeowners are physicians, one of whom can walk to his practice in downtown Bethesda.
“When needed, the dedicated home offices allow both physicians to work from home in spaces with calming natural light,” the studio said.
“Its location – easily walkable to downtown amenities and robust public transit – supports a connected pattern of work and family life.”

Other homes in Maryland include a restored carriage house by Colleen Healey Architecture that features colourful facade panels and a family home by Ziger Snead clad in stone shingles, charred wood and weathering steel.
Design architect: Desai Chia ArchitectureArchitect of record: Thomson & Cooke Architects

items.title: Gordon Ramsay to host Top Gear as show revived after Flintoff crash
paragraphs: 'Top Gear is back': Gordon Ramsay announced as new host
TV chef Gordon Ramsay is to lead the new presenting line-up on BBC motoring show Top Gear, which is being revived four years after it was last on air.
Ramsay will take the driving seat alongside as yet unnamed co-presenters when the show starts filming next year. It will return to screens in 2028.

The long-running programme has been off air since 2022, when co-host Andrew Flintoff suffered serious facial and rib injuries after his open-topped three-wheeled car overturned at the show's test-track.

In a statement announcing his new role, Ramsay said he wants to bring "a fresh energy and ambition" to the show's formula of being "surprising, entertaining and [with] just the right amount of chaos".
Andrew Flintoff, Paddy McGuinness and Chris Harris hosted the show before it was rested
Top Gear began in 1977 and became one of the BBC's biggest hits in the hands of Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May in the 2000s.
They were replaced by hosts including Chris Evans and Friends star Matt LeBlanc, before Flintoff took over in 2018 with Paddy McGuinness and Chris Harris.
But the show was "rested" after the former cricketer's crash in December 2022.
Flintoff was dragged face-down underneath the Morgan Super 3 car for about 50 metres. "I thought I was dead," he told a Disney+ documentary last year.
The BBC apologised and paid compensation to Flintoff following his crash.
In Wednesday's statement, Ramsay said he has had a love of cars since he grew up near the Silverstone race circuit in Northamptonshire.

"I would climb over the fences and sneak in for a glimpse of the racing," he said. "That early excitement sparked a lifelong passion for cars, motor sport, beautiful design and extraordinary engineering.
"At its very best Top Gear has always been about the unexpected - surprising, entertaining and just the right amount of chaos.
"That's the spirit we want to build on, bringing a fresh energy and ambition to create something truly thrilling for a whole new generation of audiences.
"It's an incredibly exciting opportunity, and I genuinely can't wait to get started!"
Former host Richard Hammond told BBC Radio 4's PM programme that Top Gear is "a grand old BBC stalwart".

"It goes back decades. We had our tenure of it and did our thing with it and went a bit crazy with it, and it'll be another incarnation of it," he said. "And great. It's a long runner, it'll carry on."
He said that he does not doubt Ramsay's credentials as a car fan, and joked that TV chefs "love three things: cooking - well in his case four - swearing, cooking, but also big watches and cars".
Hammond was seriously injured in a crash while filming the show in 2006, but said it "doesn't have to be" a dangerous show.
The BBC asked Hammond to return to the show for the new series, he said.
"They did talk to me about it. They came to me about maybe getting involved in leading the new Top Gear, and I don't want to drag it back to what it was. That's why I didn't do it," he said.
Ramsay drove in a celebrity race in Lego-themed cars at the Las Vegas Grand Prix at the weekend
Ramsay, 60, owns an extensive collection of cars including multiple Aston Martins and Ferraris, as well as a Porsche, Land Rover and McLaren Senna.
He has also appeared on Top Gear three times as a guest - in 2002, 2006 and 2017.

The BBC's director of entertainment Ed Havard said: "Gordon's fierce and fearless approach makes him a natural fit, and we're thrilled that audiences will see him in the driving seat as the show speeds into its next exciting era."
Suzy Lamb, managing director for BBC Studios Entertainment, added: "The return of Top Gear had to feel like a real TV event and Gordon fits the bill perfectly.
"He brings passion, mischief, genuine motoring credibility, and the kind of infectious competitive streak that defines the show at its best."
She promised that it "won't be a nostalgic reboot" but will be a "bold and unmissable new chapter for the most entertaining motoring show in the world".
Comedian Jimmy Carr was rumoured to have been in talks to join the hosting line-up, but was reported on Tuesday, external to have "pulled out".
Top Gear is the second high-profile show involving Ramsay to have been announced in the past week.
He has also been confirmed to star in a revival of Hell's Kitchen on ITV, hosted by Claudia Winkleman, more than two decades after he originally appeared on the celebrity cooking programme.

items.title: Anselm Kiefer review – Holocaust-haunted forests and a glimpse into a gigantic grave
paragraphs: When the world is falling apart, the artist retreats to the studio. It’s an old story, and Anselm Kiefer has always loved the old stories, drawing for his monumental and reliably blockbuster paintings on narrative traditions ranging from Norse mythology to German Romantic poetry. So it makes sense that an artist who has dedicated his life to the question of what art means after the end of European civilisation – which is to say, after the Holocaust – should now seek out the solitude of the studio to make sense of what’s coming.

Kiefer’s exhibition at the same gallery a decade ago had the title Walhalla, after the beer hall in the sky in which dead Vikings drink away the afterlife. Now comes the more modest (you would think) subject of the artist’s studio, depicted here in a suite of lustrous landscapes and a simple wooden cabin in the forest. Rendered in flat gold leaf, the sky in these paintings gleams like a tarnished halo in an old altarpiece, while the verdigris grass pushes roughly off the canvas. Here is the place where heaven meets the earth and is transmuted – by the alchemy of this painter’s touch – into quietly numinous paintings containing elements of both.

If you can put aside the fact that Kiefer’s own studio is a vast warehouse complex on the outskirts of Paris, these paintings present a very German vision of communion with nature. They also evoke the most famous hut in modern philosophy: the Black Forest hideaway where Martin Heidegger formulated his argument that “authentic” culture must be rooted in the native landscape. The flipside of this idea, that nature is not just a scenic backdrop to human history but a living participant in it, would have, let’s just say, consequences for German painting after 1945. Here is the challenge that Kiefer has spent his career meeting: how to paint the landscape as an unspoilt refuge from society when it is littered with mass graves?

Given that his forests are haunted by these horrors, it is inevitable that a series of paintings of hunters’ lookouts, displayed back to back on trolley wheels, should call to mind camp watchtowers, their high windows like unblinking eyes. And that an eight-metre-tall canvas of a building’s interior collapsing into a bonfire of real charcoal planks (affixed to the canvas and painted with brilliant licks of flame) should imply more than the destruction of an artist’s inventory. Here is a world of fire and ash, burning so that it might be reborn. The dark glamour, the virtuoso handling of the paint and the sheer scale are seductive.

Yet the power of the studio paintings derives more from their marvellous combination of colours and textures than their symbolism. For a hermetic artist, who magpies from esoteric theories as scattered as alchemy, string theory and Kabbalah in a search for hidden correspondences that can sometimes manifest as a generalised profundity, this focus on a subject qualifies as restraint. I was wondering whether this might even herald a new and (relatively) pared-back late style when I came to a painting of a naked man resembling the artist lying in a blasted landscape, learning from the handout that it was titled (in Latin, no less) On the Third Day He Rose Again, and thought: aha. Faint hope.

It is not surprising that an octogenarian artist’s thoughts should turn to mortality, and everyone must make their own private sense of that approaching horizon. It’s your funeral, as they say. But the enormous paintings that end this show – featuring solitary men staring morosely into pits, lying in open graves, and being miraculously resurrected – link the archetypal figure of the artist to the martyrdom of Christ and the genocides of the 20th century. Even for someone as indifferent to appearing pretentious as Kiefer, this is heady stuff.

In fairness, the idea that the death of the artist might redeem humanity is – I think – intended as bleakly ironic: one man gazing blankly into what could be a mass grave is identified as Narcissus. But at worst, it seems crass. Two paintings in the same room are dedicated to the poets Paul Celan and Ezra Pound. Here it is important to know that Celan, who was Jewish, wrote the line that is quoted in Kiefer’s painting while he was imprisoned in a forced labour camp and his parents were being murdered. Pound, at this time, was living in Italy and broadcasting violently antisemitic propaganda on behalf of the fascists. It is not enough to place them together without context, as if their incorporation into Kiefer’s intricately networked but generally obscure artistic universe constitutes some magical resolution of these tensions.

Kiefer has stated his commitment to “ambivalence”, which I understand to mean that his role as an artist is to memorialise the horrors rather than unravel the contradictions that produced them. But when art reproduces the past rather than processes it, we are bound to get stuck in a loop – and we are now living through another conspiratorial age in which the profusion of myths and alternative belief systems serves to obscure clear truths.

items.title: Iranian activist whose family was targeted over VOA interview vows to continue fighting
paragraphs: Editor's note: this video was translated from the original VOA Persian video.

In an exclusive interview with VOA Persian, Iranian civil rights activist and former political prisoner Sepideh Gholian vowed to continue her fight against the Iranian regime after security forces raided her family home, arrested three of her relatives and threatened to enforce a suspended five-year prison sentence against her, citing, among other reasons, her previous interview with VOA.

Speaking again with Fahimeh Khezr-Heidari on VOA Persian’s “Omgh-e Meydan” (“Depth of Field”), Gholian recounted the raid and the torture and intimidation of her family members. She said she was prepared to return to prison but would not abandon her activism, urging the public not to forget Iran’s political prisoners. The following is an excerpt from the hourlong interview.

items.title: Switzerland Sanctions North Korean Camp Over Role in Transfer of Ukrainian Children
paragraphs: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Korean article.

North Korea is threatening to close a recently opened Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang after Bern joined sanctions that Britain and the E.U. have imposed on North Korea's Songdowon International Children's Camp.
The Swiss government opened a diplomatic office in Pyongyang in October.

Switzerland’s State Secretariat for Economic Affairs says the North Korean camp is responsible for transferring children from Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine to North Korea for "forced assimilation," which can include "indoctrination and militarized education of Ukrainian minors.”
It is not clear how many Ukrainian children have been sent to the North Korean camp. Ukrainian human rights lawyers said last year that at least two had been taken there.

In a statement carried by North Korean state media, Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, called the sanctions an “open hostile act” and a “serious infringement” on North Korean sovereignty.
Kim Yo Jong said the camp promotes “legitimate” cooperation between North Korea and Russia. She didn’t directly address the accusations that children were being forcefully relocated to the camp.

She went on to say that Pyongyang will “comprehensively reconsider the relations with unreliable Switzerland” following the sanctions on the camp and called on North Korean diplomats to take unspecified “corresponding” countermeasures.

Ukraine says more than 20,600 children have been deported or forcibly displaced since 2022, and fewer than 2,700 have returned. Russia maintains that it evacuated children from combat zones for their safety.
Switzerland has repeatedly called on Russia to return deported Ukrainian children to their families.

Switzerland's Federal Department of Foreign Affairs and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, or SECO, told VOA in a joint response on November 20 that the Songdowon International Children's Camp, located in Wonsan, North Korea, was added to Switzerland's sanctions list on November 3.
The Swiss sanctions are similar to those imposed by the U.K. and the E.U. in May, which include freezing the camps assets and prohibiting financial transactions with the facility.
The European Union has said the programs went beyond ordinary cultural exchanges and served as a vehicle for promoting pro-Russian narratives among Ukrainian children.
